b: Serge Gainsbourg biographer Jeremy Allen looks back at the life and times of an inspired French composer. Main portrait by Léo Alestro, with thanks to Ipecac

I was lucky enough to meet Jean-Claude Vannier, the French composer who died on Friday 27 November aged 83, on two separate occasions. The first time was at his apartment in the 3eme arrondissement of Paris, which was reached via the creakiest of paternoster lifts before entering into what was, by Parisian standards, a spacious room. Among its contents, everything seemed secondary to the white grand piano. It was 2011 and I was interviewing the preternaturally gifted musician and arranger for The Stool Pigeon, and while that’s 15 years ago now, I can still remember...
